column1: # Each file is named as the proof directory holds it, with its .sha256 beside it; the reverse is
# this checkout's ops/<reverse> at the proved commit. Every file, forward and reverse, must:
# - hold no COMMIT, so that run alone (psql -f) it prints its counts and rolls back: its dry run;
# - print its counts as one table of two columns, a row's name and its count;
# - be idempotent: a second run changes nothing and counts 0 everywhere.
# A forward file is pending exactly when its dry run counts a row that is not 0; deploy keeps no
# record of what it ran, as the database is that record. A row named in the third field must be
# in the dry run and count 0, or deploy stops and rolls back for a person to decide.
